# gate { #gambeta.gate }

`gate`

Gate, then rank.

The definition says a player *must have* eleven things. That is read literally: a
floor on every requirement decides who qualifies, and only qualifiers are ranked.
A weighted average alone would let a player be genuinely poor at something the
list calls a requirement and still win on volume elsewhere.

The third output, which requirement each failed player missed, is a
first-class deliverable, not diagnostics. "Haaland fails longevity" is more
informative than his rank, and it is what makes the definition arguable instead
of decreed.

## Functions

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [career_profile](#gambeta.gate.career_profile) | Pool a player's seasons into one value per requirement. |
| [failure_summary](#gambeta.gate.failure_summary) | Count how many players each requirement eliminated. |
| [qualify_and_rank](#gambeta.gate.qualify_and_rank) | Apply the floor to every requirement, then rank the qualifiers. |
| [standardise](#gambeta.gate.standardise) | Z-score every requirement across players so they share one scale. |

### career_profile { #gambeta.gate.career_profile }

```python
gate.career_profile(seasons, reqs, cfg)
```

Pool a player's seasons into one value per requirement.

Season-level requirements are averaged across the player's seasons weighted
by minutes, so a 200-minute cameo cannot swing a career. Longevity and
consistency are then derived from that same per-season series.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name    | Type                      | Description                                                                                                           | Default    |
|---------|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| seasons | pd.DataFrame              | Player-seasons whose requirement columns are already z-scored within ``(league, season)`` and league-offset adjusted. | _required_ |
| reqs    | tuple\[Requirement, ...\] | The requirement list, :data:`gambeta.needs.OUTFIELD` or ``KEEPER``.                                                   | _required_ |
| cfg     | Config                    | Supplies nothing here yet but keeps the signature uniform with the rest of the pipeline.                              | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                                                                                                       |
|--------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | pd.DataFrame | One row per player, one column per requirement, plus ``seasons`` and ``leagues`` describing the career behind it. |

### failure_summary { #gambeta.gate.failure_summary }

```python
gate.failure_summary(ranking, reqs)
```

Count how many players each requirement eliminated.

A requirement that eliminates nobody is not doing any work; one that
eliminates almost everybody is miscalibrated. Both are worth seeing.

### qualify_and_rank { #gambeta.gate.qualify_and_rank }

```python
gate.qualify_and_rank(profile, reqs, cfg, weights=None)
```

Apply the floor to every requirement, then rank the qualifiers.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name    | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                    | Default    |
|---------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| profile | pd.DataFrame               | Output of :func:`standardise`.                                                                                                                                 | _required_ |
| reqs    | tuple\[Requirement, ...\]  | The requirement list being applied.                                                                                                                            | _required_ |
| cfg     | Config                     | Supplies ``gate_percentile``.                                                                                                                                  | _required_ |
| weights | dict\[str, float\] \| None | Per-requirement weights for the ranking. Sparse: any requirement left out counts 1.0, so naming the one you care about is enough. Defaults to equal weighting. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|--------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | pd.DataFrame | Conforming to :data:`gambeta.laws.RANKING`, sorted with qualifiers first and best first within them. Non-qualifiers are retained with ``qualified=False`` and the requirements they missed listed in ``failed``. |

### standardise { #gambeta.gate.standardise }

```python
gate.standardise(profile, reqs)
```

Z-score every requirement across players so they share one scale.

Without this the gate would compare a save percentage against a per-90 rate
and the weighted mean would be dominated by whichever requirement happened to
have the largest units.
